## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

The *Yakkhapahāra Sutta* (Ud 4.4, PTS Ud 39) is a discourse in the *Udāna* collection of the Pali Canon. The text recounts an episode in which a spirit (*yakkha*) delivers a violent blow to the head of the Venerable Sāriputta while he sits in meditation.

Full parallels to the sutta are preserved in the Chinese Āgamas, specifically two *Saṁyuktāgama* versions: SA 1330 and SA2 329 (both titled 害及無害), alongside a resembling parallel in the *Ekottarikāgama* (EA 48.6). Automated cross-language text alignment by DharmaNexus confirms close correspondences to these Chinese collections, registering high-scoring alignments with T 99 (*Saṁyuktāgama*), T 125 (*Ekottarikāgama*), and T 100 (the alternative *Saṁyuktāgama* translation) [DharmaNexus]. Passages and verses from the sutta also parallel verses in various versions of the *Udānavarga* (UV 31, UVS 31, Uv Kg 31, T 212.32, and T 213.31) and the *Theragāthā* (Thag 2.36) [DharmaNexus].

Within Pali literature, the sutta is cited or referenced in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37), the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2, Pe 8), and the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.1.1). DharmaNexus records widespread internal Pali text reuse, identifying 226 matching passages across 27 texts; its most substantial continuous overlap occurs with the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*, alongside shared phraseology in the *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), and other canonical and commentarial texts [DharmaNexus].
